content:
Apple TV September kicks off the season with a string of eye-catching new releases, including a film starring Ryan Reynolds, a new season of "Slow Horses," and a comedy series starring Matthew McConaughey. Below is Apple TV's new content for September.

Mayday

  • Date: September 4
  • Type: Film
  • Genre: Action comedy

Ryan Reynolds and Kim Hyun-joong team up in "Mayday," a genre-bending, fast-paced action comedy that turns the spy thriller on its head. At the height of the Cold War, US Army ace pilot Lt. Troy "Assassin" Kelly (played by Reynolds) is sent deep into Russian territory on a top-secret mission that goes awry, leaving him stranded behind enemy lines. Troy is discovered by a stern-looking former KGB agent, Nikolai Ustinov (played by Hyun-joong), who is obsessed with American culture and assumes the worst is about to happen—but can this unlikely alliance save Troy and forge an unexpected friendship?

Last Seen

  • Date: September 9
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Thriller

Eleven years ago, Detective Ian Ridley (played by Patrick Balmain)'s world fell apart when his young daughter Maggie mysteriously vanished. Now working as a police dispatcher, the only thing keeping him going is his refusal to accept that his daughter may be gone forever. When he receives a call for help from a young woman he believes to be Maggie, he will stop at nothing to find her and piece his shattered family back together.

Slow Horses (Season 6)

  • Date: September 16
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Spy thriller

This darkly humorous spy drama follows a group of British intelligence officers who, after career-ending blunders, have been banished to MI5's "slough department." Led by their brilliant but foul-tempered legendary boss, Jackson Lamb—played by Oscar winner Sir Gary Oldman—they navigate the smoke and mirrors of the spy world, striving to protect Britain from the forces of evil.

Brothers

  • Date: September 23
  • Type: Series
  • Genre: Comedy

"Brothers" stars Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson as dramatised versions of themselves. When a long-buried secret is revealed—that the two may actually be half-brothers—their lifelong friendship is thrown into chaos. After Woody daughter wedding falls through, he takes his whole family to Austin, planning to settle in on Matthew farm. What was supposed to be a healing trip turns sour when Matthew mother, Ma Mac (played by Holland Taylor), accidentally lets slip that the two old friends might really be half-brothers, a secret long buried. Woody turns the farm upside down to chase the truth, while Matthew faces an identity crisis of his own—possibly running for governor of Texas. Ultimately, the story is a touching, wildly funny tale about friendship, family, fame and fortune, and the blurry line between myth and reality.

New episodes: "Ted Lasso," "Dark Matter," and more

September will also continue to roll out new episodes of currently airing Apple TV series, including:

  • "Silo": Dystopian sci-fi series, airing through September 4
  • "Women in Blue": Spanish-language crime drama, airing through September 30
  • "Ted Lasso": Comedy starring Jason Sudeikis, airing through October 7
  • "Dark Matter": Sci-fi series starring Joel Edgerton, airing through October 30

Among Apple TV's new September releases, which one are you planning to watch? Let us know in the comments.

Apple TV monthly subscription is US$12.99, and discounted bundles are also available through Apple One.
